The lack of interoperable standards significantly impacts compliance with Art. 50 II for both synthetic data and fact-checking systems by creating a fragmented implementation landscape. In synthetic data generation, the absence of cross-platform marking formats means that watermarks or labels designed for one system may not be detectable by another, violating the requirement for interoperability. This fragmentation complicates the integration of synthetic data from multiple sources and hinders the ability to utilize data across different AI systems.

In fact-checking systems, the lack of unified marking approaches for outputs that combine text, images, and video further exacerbates compliance challenges. Existing provenance frameworks do not adequately support the interleaved nature of human and AI contributions, making it difficult to maintain clear provenance chains necessary for machine-readable marking. This results in operational difficulties, as the human editorial process can destroy the marking signals required for compliance, thus undermining the regulatory intent of Art. 50 II. Overall, the absence of interoperable standards leads to substantial impediments for organizations striving to meet the compliance obligations set forth by the regulation.
